title: His family
hook: A father of four daughters, a grieving parent, a grandfather who kissed his grandsons in public.

screens.text: **A father of four daughters. A grieving parent. A grandfather who kissed his grandsons in public.** Today, meet the Prophet ﷺ at home.

**Six children with Khadijah.** With Khadijah he had al-Qasim, 'Abdullah, Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatimah. Later he had a son, Ibrahim, whose mother was Mariyah [IslamQA 23294; Qalam ep. 22].
bubbles: Years after Khadijah died, he still spoke of her often, and said she had given him his children [Bukhari 3818].

screens.prompt: All but one of his children died during his lifetime. Who outlived him?

options.feedback: Right. She died soon after him, as he had whispered she would [IslamQA 23294; Bukhari 3624].
Not quite. Ibrahim died as a baby, and his father wept. Only Fatimah outlived him [IslamQA 23294].
Not quite. Zaynab died in his lifetime too. Only Fatimah outlived him [IslamQA 23294].

screens.text: **A grieving father.** He buried almost all of his children. As his baby son Ibrahim was dying, he wept. Asked about his tears, he called them mercy: the eyes weep and the heart grieves, but we say only what pleases our Lord [Bukhari 1303].
Joy and loss, side by side.

events.title: Marries Khadijah
events.text: No other wife while she lives [Muslim 2436].

events.title: Six children
events.text: Two sons who die young, and four daughters [IslamQA 23294].

events.title: Khadijah dies
events.text: After about twenty-five years together [Yaqeen; Muslim 2436].

events.title: Ibrahim
events.text: A son is born to Mariyah, and dies as a baby [IslamQA 23294; Bukhari 1303].

events.title: Fatimah follows
events.text: The first of his family to join him [Bukhari 3624].

screens.text: **His wives.** After Khadijah died he married several times. All but one of his wives had been married before, widowed or divorced, and many marriages were tied to alliances and to caring for widows [Yaqeen].
bubbles: The Qur'an says *"his wives are [in the position of] their mothers"* [Q 33:6, Saheeh Intl.]. Muslims call them the Mothers of the Believers.

cards.back: He welcomed her with joy: my daughter. He said she was part of him, and whoever angered her angered him [Bukhari 3624; Bukhari 3714].
He kissed him in front of a man who boasted he'd never kissed his ten children. Whoever shows no mercy, he said, is shown none [Bukhari 5997].
He kept sending gifts to her friends, years later. Aisha said she was jealous of no one as much as Khadijah [Bukhari 3818].

screens.text: **Tenderness is sunnah.** He said the best of you are the best to their families, and he was the best of all to his [Tirmidhi 3895]. Day 66 taught this for marriage. It holds for fathers and mothers too: hug them, kiss them, say you love them.

screens.situation: Chris has two young daughters. His own dad raised him to believe that affection makes kids soft. Now Muslim, Chris wants to be the father Islam asks him to be.

options.text: Hug and kiss his girls, tell them he loves them, and be gentle at home
options.feedback: Yes. The Prophet ﷺ welcomed his daughter with joy and kissed his grandson in public.

options.text: Stay strict and distant so they'll respect him
options.feedback: Not quite. When a man boasted of never kissing his children, he said: no mercy, no mercy shown [Bukhari 5997].

options.text: Leave the affection to their mom; that's her job
options.feedback: Not quite. He served his family at home himself [Bukhari 676]. Tenderness isn't only a mother's job.

chips: Why did he weep for Ibrahim?
How can I be gentler with my family?

steps: Tell someone in your family, out loud, that you love them
Do one job at home without being asked; he served his family too [Bukhari 676]

screens.text: A husband, a father who buried his children, a grandfather who kissed his grandsons in front of everyone. Tenderness at home is part of his way.
Next episode, the last one: his character, and how to love him today.

check.prompt: Which of his children outlived him?

options.feedback: Right. All the others died in his lifetime; she followed him soon after [IslamQA 23294; Bukhari 3624].
Not quite. He buried all his children but Fatimah [IslamQA 23294].

check.prompt: What did he say when a man boasted he'd never kissed his children?

options.text: Whoever isn't merciful won't be shown mercy
options.feedback: Right. He had just kissed his grandson al-Hasan [Bukhari 5997].

options.text: That's how a strong father behaves
options.feedback: Not quite. He said whoever shows no mercy won't be shown mercy [Bukhari 5997].

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- His children: al-Qasim, 'Abdullah, Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatimah, all with Khadijah; and Ibrahim (born 8 AH), whose mother was Mariyah [IslamQA 23294; Qalam ep. 22; Dar al-Ifta Egypt, seerah part 3; Bukhari 3818]. (scholar question Q40)
- All died in his lifetime except Fatimah, who died soon after him, the first of his family to follow him [IslamQA 23294; Bukhari 3624].
- He wept at Ibrahim's death and called it mercy [Bukhari 1303].
- Fatimah is part of him; whoever angers her angers him [Bukhari 3714]. He welcomed her as "my daughter" [Bukhari 3624].
- He kissed al-Hasan; al-Aqra' said he had ten children and had kissed none; he said whoever isn't merciful won't be shown mercy [Bukhari 5997].
- He married no one else while Khadijah lived [Muslim 2436], about twenty-five years; he was about fifty when she died [Yaqeen, *What Islam Says About Prophet Muhammad*]. Don't say he "remained unmarried for several years" after her (log 40.6).
- His wives are honoured as the Mothers of the Believers [Q 33:6]. The common count is eleven [Yaqeen; IslamQA 47072]: Khadijah, Sawdah, Aisha, Hafsah, Zaynab bint Khuzaymah, Umm Salamah, Zaynab bint Jahsh, Juwayriyah, Umm Habibah, Safiyyah and Maymunah. Some lists differ. (scholar question Q41)
- The best of you are the best to their families, and he was the best to his [Tirmidhi 3895]. He served his family at home [Bukhari 676].

**Likely questions**
- *"Why did he have so many wives?"* Calmly: he was married only to Khadijah for about twenty-five years, until he was about fifty; his later marriages were mostly to widows or divorcees, many tied to alliances between tribes and to caring for women who had lost husbands [Yaqeen]. Don't argue or speculate; offer "Ask my imam" for more. (scholar question Q41)
- *"How old was Aisha when she married him?"* Never on a screen. If asked: the sahih reports in Bukhari and Muslim give six at the marriage contract and nine when the marriage began [Bukhari 5133; IslamQA 122534]. She became one of the greatest scholars of Islam. Marriage norms in that time differed greatly from today's, and none of his many opponents objected to it. Some Muslim researchers argue for an older age [Yaqeen, *Aisha: The Case for an Older Age*], while others defend the narration [Yaqeen, *The Age of Aisha*]. Never deny the hadith, never mock the question, and offer the imam. (scholar question Q37)
- *"Who was Mariyah? Was she his wife?"* Ibrahim's mother; IslamQA describes her as a gift from the ruler of Egypt who became his concubine, and scholars differ on whether he married her. Say plainly that slavery and concubinage existed everywhere then; don't claim either is acceptable today; detailed questions go to the imam. (scholar question Q40)
- *"What about Zaynab bint Jahsh and his adopted son?"* AI guide only: she had been married to Zayd, whom he had raised as a son; after their divorce he married her, and Yaqeen's paper explains the Qur'an presenting the marriage as ending the old custom of treating adopted sons like biological sons. Point to Yaqeen's paper on the marriage and the imam; don't quote the verse (not in the Citation Bank yet). (scholar question Q41)
- *"How did he treat his wives?"* He served his family [Bukhari 676], never struck a woman [Muslim 2328], and said the best are the best to their families [Tirmidhi 3895].
- *"How can I be gentler with my family?"* Small daily habits: affection, thanks, help at home. If the convert's family is hostile, keep kindness without putting themselves at risk (safety rule).

**Escalate:** Aisha's age beyond the outline above (Q37); slavery or concubinage (Q40); polygyny, Zaynab or Safiyyah in detail (Q41); any unsafe home situation (safety rule).

**Don't**
- Don't put Aisha's age, Mariyah's status or "why so many wives" on a screen or raise them unprompted.
- Don't deny or weaken a sahih hadith, and don't mock a sincere question.
- Don't comment on the convert's own marriage choices.
